reproduction_status: not reproduced; records describe what the page shows
notes: Eight figures and eight tables. Every one was seen on a page proxy or a crop. The text layer scrambles symbol rows and drops column headers, so cell values below come from the image.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the whole workflow so the reader sees the order before the prose starts.
visualization_observations.summary: Four colored panels inside one dashed border, read left to right, with a legend of three rounded labels at the right marked Task 1, Task 2, Task 3. Task 4 has no color. Green is data preprocessing, yellow is the price prediction model with the LSTM and the parameter choice, orange is the investment strategy model and is the first place the paper says the program is divided into 6 cases and names the ideal point method, blue is strategy evaluation with 10 metrics and 4 benchmark strategies, pink is sensitivity with the 2 result metrics and 5 strategy metrics split into two boxes. Arrows run from preprocessing down to prediction, from prediction right to strategy, and from strategy right to both evaluation and sensitivity. Caption: Figure 1: Modeling framework.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The figure states the pipeline and three facts the bullet list omits: six cases, the ideal point method, and the 2-against-5 metric split.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Arrow labels are small; the direction was read, the wording on the arrows was not.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the LSTM cell so the gate equations have a picture.
visualization_observations.summary: A standard LSTM cell diagram. Left block labeled Data Preprocessing over Input Vector, right block titled LSTM MODULE with gates marked, two green boxes marked A, and the usual cell-state line across the top. Caption: Figure 2: Workflow of LSTM.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The figure shows the cell the equations describe. It adds no result.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Internal gate labels are too small to transcribe.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show how the sliding window moves.
visualization_observations.summary: A strip of day boxes. An input window covers days up to day t and an output arrow leaves at the right edge. Caption: Figure 3: The process of Sliding Window Algorithm. The picture agrees with the prose: d days in, one day out.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The window slides one day at a time and emits one prediction.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The training length d' is named in the prose and is not marked on the figure.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the forecast against the realized price.
visualization_observations.summary: Two panels side by side. (a) Price of gold, (b) Price of bitcoin. Each has two lines, predicted and real, in orange and blue, and in both panels the two lines lie almost on top of each other across 2016 to 2021. Gold rises from roughly 1,200 to about 1,800 with a spike near 2,000. Bitcoin stays low for years and then climbs past 60,000. Caption: Figure 4: Predicted price vs real prices. The sentence under it says the predictions are proven good by comparing the curves.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The forecast tracks the realized price closely in both panels. The figure does not show error bars or a naive baseline.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Legend colors were not transcribed. Axis values are eye readings.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show when bitcoin was bought and sold.
visualization_observations.summary: One panel, January 2017 to January 2018, with a legend of bitcoin, buy, sell and value. What is drawn is the price rising from near 1,000 to near 20,000. No buy marker and no sell marker is visible. Caption: Figure 5: Date to buy or sell bitcoin, from Jan.1, 2017 to Jan.1, 2018. The caption promises dates the figure does not show.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The figure shows the bitcoin price over that year. It does not show the trade dates its caption names.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Markers could be present but smaller than the crop resolves. None was seen.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show the portfolio value over the whole period.
visualization_observations.summary: One line, daily asset value, from late 2016 to late 2021. It climbs in steps, with long flat stretches and sharp rises, and finishes just under 15,000. The prose says the value is discounted by the closing price. Caption: Figure 6: Curve of daily asset value.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The portfolio ends near 14,000 to 15,000, consistent with the stated 14,325.13.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The final tick was read by eye, not from a data file.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Compare the five strategies on one axis.
visualization_observations.summary: Five curves on a log axis labeled log(value), ticks 2.2 to 5.2, dates from 2016/9/11 to about 2021/8/16. Legend entries are printed our(our asset), gold(gold asset), bitcoin(bitcoin asset), ideal(ideal asset), rule(rule asset), with no space before the parenthesis. At the right edge ideal ends just under 5.2, our just below it, rule near 4.5, bitcoin near 4.2, gold flat near 3.0 to 3.2. On this axis our and ideal finish close together. Table 4 puts ideal's annualized return at 1406.66 percent against our 266.36 percent. The log compresses exactly the gap the table reports, and the caption does not say the axis is logarithmic. Caption: Figure 7: Comparison of the curve of daily asset value among strategies.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: All five strategies are plotted. The figure does not support a claim that our strategy finishes near the ideal one.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Justify the standard deviation inside the Sharpe ratio by showing normality.
visualization_observations.summary: Five panels, (a) our asset, (b) gold asset, (c) bitcoin asset, (d) ideal asset, (e) rule asset. Each carries the same legend, a normal curve and bars for the yield rate, with density on the vertical. Panels (a), (b), (d) and (e) are thin spikes at zero, far sharper than the normal curve drawn over them. Only (c), bitcoin, makes a broad mound. The sentence above says the plot is there to make sure the Sharpe ratio is valid. The sentence below says all five are subject to normal distribution. Four of the five panels do not show that.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The yield distribution is plotted for all five strategies. The normality claim holds, if anywhere, only for bitcoin.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The crop ends at the subtitles of panels (d) and (e); the caption line was taken from the text layer.

visualization_observations.summary: Two columns of symbol and definition. Left column runs b, C, C-tilde, d, d', f, h, i, L, l, M, m, o. Right column runs P, r, S, t, V, v, W, w, alpha, epsilon, lambda, sigma, omega. Two rows collide: f and o are both defined as output function of forget gate, and i is defined as input function of forget gate. The text layer had shifted every symbol down a row; the image is the source. Caption: Table 1: Symbol list.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The table lists the notation. It contradicts itself on f, i and o.

visualization_observations.summary: Ten rows in two groups of five. Dates and corrected prices: 12/23/16 at 1132.975, 12/30/16 at 1148.45, 12/22/17 at 1271.975, 12/29/17 at 1301.525, 12/24/18 at 1263.075, 12/31/18 at 1280.95, 12/24/19 at 1496.8, 12/31/19 at 1520.925, 12/24/20 at 1874.65, 12/31/20 at 1915.4. Every missing trading day falls on a late-December date. Caption: Table 2: Trading days with missing gold price and corrected gold price.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Ten gold prices were filled, all of them around the year-end holidays.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: The text layer and the count agree. The individual cells were not re-read from a crop.

visualization_observations.summary: Three pairs of columns: d, d' and lambda, each with its MAPE. d runs 7, 10, 13, 15, 20 with MAPE 0.007320101, 0.007261552, 0.011110205, 0.010985684, 0.010590555. d' runs 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 with MAPE 0.010315979, 0.012500496, 0.007261552, 0.008998699, 0.007450314. lambda runs 0.0005, 0.0007, 0.001, 0.0015, 0.002 with MAPE 0.008678837, 0.008465359, 0.007261552, 0.009933032, 0.010285589. The minimum in each pair is bold and equals 0.007261552, and each bold cell sits on the initial value: d = 10, d' = 5, lambda = 0.001. Hidden size and epoch are not scanned. Caption: Table 3: MAPE values of the price prediction of gold.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Under this scan the starting values give the lowest MAPE. The scan never tests a value away from the start as a winner.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Compare the five strategies on the ten metrics.
visualization_observations.summary: Two five-column tables, one per group of metrics, read earlier from p20-tab.jpg. The prose compares our strategy only with the rivals it beats: risk against the bitcoin strategy, return against the gold strategy and the rule strategy. The ideal strategy's annualized return of 1406.66 percent and its Sharpe ratio of 0.2955 are printed in the table and not mentioned in the comment. Our annualized return is 266.36 percent and our Sharpe ratio is 0.0791.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: The table ranks five strategies. The prose reports a subset of that ranking.
visualization_observations.missing_or_unverified: Full cell transcription is in the G0 notes, not repeated here.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show how trading behavior changes with the gold commission.
visualization_observations.summary: Columns v_g, v_b, V_g, V_b, V_a against gold commission from 0 to 4 percent, bitcoin held at 2 percent. Rows: 0.7622, 0.8286, 6, 52, 58; then 0.6333, 0.8391, 10, 40, 50; then 0.9497, 0.8307, 2, 38, 40; then a dash, 0.8223, 0, 40, 40; then a dash, 0.8255, 0, 40, 40. v_b stays between 0.8223 and 0.8391. V_g goes 6, 10, 2, 0, 0, so it doubles before it vanishes. The dash appears exactly where the gold count is zero. Caption: Table 5: Trading behaviors under different commissions of gold.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Gold trading stops entirely at 3 and 4 percent. The average gold percentage does not rise steadily.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show net profit and win rate against the gold commission.
visualization_observations.summary: Gold commission, net profit, win rate: 0 percent gives 10874.24 and 0.2745; 1 percent gives 14325.13 and 0.381; 2 percent gives 13069.35 and 0.4474; 3 percent gives 14587.49 and 0.4103; 4 percent gives 10865.78 and 0.4615. The largest profit sits at 3 percent, not at the cheapest commission. The 0 and 4 percent profits differ by 8.46. The prose says the net profit remains the same.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Profit moves by thousands across the sweep. The win rate ends higher than it starts but dips at 3 percent.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show how trading behavior changes with the bitcoin commission.
visualization_observations.summary: Same five columns against bitcoin commission from 1 to 5 percent, gold held at 1 percent. Rows: 0.5829, 0.7921, 12, 48, 60; then 0.6333, 0.8391, 10, 40, 50; then 0.7622, 0.8286, 12, 42, 54; then 0.785, 0.8255, 8, 44, 52; then 0.7906, 0.8245, 8, 32, 40. The 2 percent row matches Table 5's 1 percent row exactly, so the two sweeps share their one overlapping cell. The 4 percent row prints 0.785 with three decimals where every other percentage prints four. v_g rises the whole way. The counts do not fall steadily.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: A higher bitcoin commission pushes a larger share of each gold purchase. It does not reduce every count monotonically.

visualization_observations.analytical_purpose: Show net profit and win rate against the bitcoin commission.
visualization_observations.summary: Bitcoin commission, net profit, win rate: 1 percent gives 11632.52 and 0.4583; 2 percent gives 14325.13 and 0.381; 3 percent gives 2774.01 and 0.2745; 4 percent gives 1641.35 and 0.2954; 5 percent gives 1583.01 and 0.303. The 2 percent row repeats the headline result, so it is the base case. From 2 to 3 percent the profit falls to about a fifth and then flattens. The win rate falls for three steps and rises for two. The prose says it shows a decreasing trend.
visualization_observations.exact_claim_supported: Profit collapses once the bitcoin commission passes 2 percent. The win rate does not decrease throughout.

cross_checks: Figure 7's log axis compresses the gap that Table 4 prints in full.
Figure 8's normality claim fails on four of its five panels, and the Sharpe ratio in section 5.1 depends on that claim.
Figure 5's caption names buy and sell dates that the plotted curves do not mark.
Table 6's profit column contradicts the sentence directly above it.
Table 8's win-rate column turns up at the end, against the sentence that calls it decreasing.
Table 5 at 1 percent and Table 7 at 2 percent are the same portfolio and their five numbers match.
Table 1 defines both f and o as the forget gate's output and defines i as the forget gate's input.
